newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia gets drafts from three Paris Club countries.
newsitem.headline: Russia gets drafts from three Paris Club countries.

text.p: Russia has received draft agreements from Belgium, Austria and France on rescheduling its official debts, a finance ministry official said on Tuesday.
Sergei Storchak, head of the foreign debt service department, told Reuters it was too soon to say when meetings would be held with officials from these countries.
Russia and the Paris Club agreed in April to reschedule $40 billion of Russian debt for up to 25 years, including a grace period of six years.
Russia is now negotiating with individual members of the Paris Club within the framework of this overall agreement.
In September a Russian delegation met Swiss and German officials to agree the exact amount of debts owed these countries and the schedule of payments.
The two sides had settled all the legal issues, but financial problems were still to be solved, Storchak said. He refused to state how much Russia owed any of the countries.
